description: Identify and characterize multimodal AI systems and the four core problems of multimodal machine learning - representation, alignment, fusion, and translation, including Foundations of Multimodality, What multimodal AI is and isn't, The four core problems: representation, alignment, fusion, translation, Why now: from connectors to native multimodality.

Build cross-modal representations using contrastive and self-supervised methods, and evaluate them via zero-shot transfer and cross-modal retrieval, including Cross-Modal Representation Learning, Contrastive learning and the InfoNCE objective.

Design and implement fusion architectures (cross-attention, latent bottlenecks, connector modules) that combine heterogeneous modalities, including Cross-attention as the fusion engine, Perceiver and latent bottlenecks, Q-Former and projection connectors, Flamingo: gated cross-attention.

Apply vision-language and unified multimodal architectures (LLaVA, BLIP-2, Flamingo, and unified token/diffusion-transformer families) and instruction-tune them, including Flamingo: gated cross-attention, Unified-token decoder-only models (Chameleon, Emu3), The discrete-token understanding gap.

Apply multimodal techniques to non-image modalities - speech, audio, video, 3D, and embodied agents - and to cross-modal generation, including Speech and Audio, Audio as a modality, ASR and Whisper, Audio understanding and audio-LMs, TTS and speech/music generation, Cross-Modal Generation, Text-to-audio and music generation, Video, Why video is hard: temporal structure.

Engineer multimodal reasoning, agent, and retrieval systems, and address the input-size and latency challenges of deploying them, including Multimodal Reasoning, Agents and Retrieval, Multimodal reasoning and thinking with images, Computer-use and GUI agents, Cross-modal retrieval and multimodal RAG, Quantization for VLMs, serving multimodal models.

Evaluate multimodal systems with appropriate benchmarks and protocols, recognizing saturation and the migrating frontier, and run hallucination and grounding diagnostics, including Why evaluation is hard, the saturation story (MMMU-Pro) and Where the frontier moved: video, OCR, audio, unified eval.

Analyze the safety, provenance, bias, and privacy issues specific to multimodal AI - deepfakes, watermarking, and biometric data, including Safety, Provenance and Frontiers / Course Wrap, The multimodal risk surface, deepfakes and synthetic media, Provenance and watermarking (C2PA), Biometric and facial privacy, bias across modalities.
